# ghost_user_ssh_signing_key (Resource)

Manages an SSH signing key of the authenticated user (the owner of the provider's token). Ghost uses signing keys to verify SSH-signed commits; they don't grant git access. Ghost can't edit a signing key, so changing the title or the key replaces it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Adds a key to the token owner's account for verifying SSH-signed commits.
# Sign with: git -c gpg.format=ssh -c user.signingkey=~/.ssh/id_ed25519 commit -S
resource "ghost_user_ssh_signing_key" "laptop" {
  title = "Laptop"
  key   = file("~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) The public key in OpenSSH format, e.g. `file("~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub")`. Ghost stores only `<type> <base64>`, so the comment and surrounding whitespace are ignored: changing them updates the state without touching the key. Any other change forces a new key.
- `title` (String) A name for the key, up to 100 characters. Changing it forces a new key.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the key was added, in ISO 8601.
- `fingerprint` (String) The key's SHA256 fingerprint, as `ssh-keygen -lf` prints it, e.g. `SHA256:y0mi…`. Ghost reports it as the `keyId` of a signed commit's verification.
- `id` (String) The numeric ID of the key.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A signing key is imported by its numeric ID, from
# GET /api/v3/user/ssh_signing_keys.
terraform import ghost_user_ssh_signing_key.laptop 42
```
